name: Muscles
note: Major skeletal muscles. "origin" and "insertion" become links to the skeleton (see linkTypes in manifest.json). Ids match data-id attributes in assets/svg/muscles-anterior.svg.

groups.name: Head & jaw
groups.summary: The chewing muscles that close and grind the jaw.

groups.name: Neck
groups.summary: Muscles that turn and steady the head and move the hyoid and larynx for swallowing.

groups.name: Shoulder & upper back
groups.summary: Muscles that move the shoulder blade and the arm at the shoulder.

groups.name: Chest wall & breathing
groups.summary: Muscles on and between the ribs, plus the diaphragm, the main muscle of breathing.

groups.name: Abdomen & core
groups.summary: The layered abdominal wall and pelvic floor that brace the trunk and support the organs.

groups.name: Back
groups.summary: Deep muscles that hold the spine upright. They sit behind the spine, so they are listed but not drawn in the front view.

groups.name: Upper arm
groups.summary: Muscles that bend and straighten the elbow.

groups.name: Forearm & hand
groups.summary: Muscles that move the wrist, fingers and thumb.

groups.name: Hip & buttock
groups.summary: Muscles that flex, extend and steady the hip.

groups.name: Thigh
groups.summary: The quadriceps in front, the adductors on the inside and the hamstrings behind.

groups.name: Quadriceps
groups.summary: Four muscles on the front of the thigh joining in one tendon over the kneecap. They are the only muscles that straighten the knee.

issues.name: Quadriceps strain
issues.note: Sudden pain at the front of the thigh when sprinting or kicking.

issues.name: Quadriceps tendon rupture
issues.note: Usually an older adult falling with the knee bent, then unable to straighten the leg. It is urgent.

groups.name: Lower leg
groups.summary: Muscles that lift, point and tilt the foot and move the toes.

structures.name: Temporalis
structures.originNote: The temporal fossa on the side of the skull
structures.insertionNote: Coronoid process of the mandible
structures.summary: A fan-shaped chewing muscle filling the temple. You can feel it tighten when you clench your teeth.

issues.name: Tension headache
issues.note: Tight, tender temples from clenching or stress.

issues.name: Teeth grinding (bruxism)
issues.note: Grinding at night overworks it, causing a morning jaw ache and headache.

structures.name: Masseter
structures.originNote: The zygomatic arch
structures.insertionNote: Outer surface of the ramus and angle of the jaw
structures.summary: The main chewing muscle, from the cheekbone to the angle of the jaw. For its size it is one of the strongest muscles in the body.

issues.name: Jaw muscle pain
issues.note: Aching cheeks and jaw from clenching, grinding or chewing gum; often part of a TMJ disorder.

structures.name: Sternocleidomastoid
structures.originNote: Top of the sternum (sternal head) and inner clavicle (clavicular head)
structures.insertionNote: Mastoid process behind the ear and the base of the skull
actions: Turns the head to the opposite side
Tilts the head toward the same shoulder
Bends the neck forward (both sides together)
Helps lift the ribcage in hard breathing
structures.summary: The prominent diagonal strap at the side of the neck, from behind the ear to the top of the breastbone. It divides the neck into front and back triangles.

issues.name: Wry neck (torticollis)
issues.note: Spasm pulls the head to one side. In babies it can be present from birth.

issues.name: Neck strain
issues.note: Pain and stiffness after a jolt or sleeping awkwardly.

structures.name: Suprahyoid muscles
structures.originNote: Inner jaw, chin and the mastoid and styloid processes of the temporal bone
actions: Lift the hyoid and larynx when you swallow
structures.summary: Four small muscles forming the floor of the mouth, slinging the hyoid up toward the jaw and skull.

members.name: Digastric
members.note: Two bellies joined by a tendon that loops through a sling on the hyoid.

members.name: Mylohyoid
members.note: A thin sheet forming the floor of the mouth.

members.name: Geniohyoid
members.note: From the inside of the chin to the hyoid.

members.name: Stylohyoid
members.note: From the styloid process of the temporal bone.

issues.name: Swallowing problems
issues.note: Weakness after a stroke or with nerve conditions can make swallowing unsafe. Coughing or choking on food needs assessment.

structures.name: Infrahyoid (strap) muscles
structures.originNote: Back of the manubrium, and the top edge of the shoulder blade (omohyoid)
actions: Pull the hyoid and larynx back down after swallowing
Steady the hyoid so the tongue and jaw can work
structures.summary: Thin strap muscles running down the front of the neck from the hyoid to the sternum and shoulder blade, covering the thyroid and windpipe.

members.name: Sternohyoid
members.note: From the sternum to the hyoid.

members.name: Sternothyroid
members.note: From the sternum to the thyroid cartilage.

members.name: Thyrohyoid
members.note: From the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid.

members.name: Omohyoid
members.note: Two bellies; it slips under the sternocleidomastoid to the top of the shoulder blade.

issues.name: Tightness after neck surgery
issues.note: They are parted in thyroid surgery and can feel tight while healing.

structures.name: Trapezius
structures.originNote: Base of the skull, the nuchal ligament and the spinous processes of C7–T12
structures.insertionNote: Outer third of the clavicle, the acromion and the spine of the scapula
actions: Rotates the shoulder blade so the arm can reach overhead
structures.summary: A large diamond-shaped muscle of the upper back and neck. From the front you only see its upper fibres, which form the slope from neck to shoulder.

issues.name: Neck and shoulder tension
issues.note: Tight, tender knots between the neck and shoulder, often from desk work and stress.

issues.name: Tension headache
issues.note: A tight trapezius and neck can refer pain to the back of the head.

structures.name: Deltoid
structures.originNote: Outer third of the clavicle, the acromion and the spine of the scapula
structures.insertionNote: Deltoid tuberosity, halfway down the outer humerus
actions: Lifts the arm out to the side
Front fibres raise the arm forward
structures.summary: The rounded cap of the shoulder, shaped like the Greek letter delta (Δ). A common site for vaccinations.

issues.name: Deltoid strain
issues.note: Pain on lifting after heavy or repetitive overhead work.

issues.name: Axillary nerve injury
issues.note: After a shoulder dislocation: a numb patch on the outer shoulder and weakness lifting the arm.

structures.name: Rotator cuff
structures.originNote: Front and back surfaces of the shoulder blade
structures.insertionNote: Greater and lesser tubercles at the top of the humerus
actions: Hold the ball of the humerus in its shallow socket
Rotate and help lift the arm
structures.summary: Four muscles from the shoulder blade whose tendons merge into a cuff around the head of the humerus. Most of them lie on the back of the shoulder blade.

members.name: Supraspinatus
members.note: Starts lifting the arm out to the side. The most commonly torn.

members.name: Infraspinatus
members.note: Turns the arm outward.

members.name: Teres minor
members.note: Turns the arm outward.

members.name: Subscapularis
members.note: On the front of the shoulder blade, against the ribs. Turns the arm inward.

issues.name: Rotator cuff tendinopathy
issues.note: Pain on the outer shoulder when lifting the arm, worse at night.

issues.name: Rotator cuff tear
issues.note: Weakness lifting the arm after a fall, or gradually with age. It may need imaging.

issues.name: Impingement
issues.note: A painful arc when raising the arm, roughly between shoulder height and overhead.

structures.name: Rhomboids
structures.originNote: Spinous processes of C7–T5
structures.insertionNote: Inner (medial) border of the shoulder blade
structures.summary: Two flat muscles between the spine and the shoulder blade, under the trapezius.

members.name: Rhomboid major
members.note: From T2–T5.

members.name: Rhomboid minor
members.note: From C7–T1.

issues.name: Pain between the shoulder blades
issues.note: Aching from posture or a sudden strain. Pain here can also come from the neck, the heart or the gallbladder.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi
structures.originNote: Lower thoracic spine, the thoracolumbar fascia, the iliac crest and the lowest ribs
structures.insertionNote: Floor of the groove at the front of the upper humerus
actions: Pulls the arm down and back
structures.summary: The broadest muscle of the back, sweeping from the lower spine and pelvis up into the armpit. From the front only its edge shows along the side of the chest.

issues.name: Lat strain
issues.note: Pain along the side of the back or in the armpit after pulling or throwing.

structures.name: Pectoralis major
structures.originNote: Inner clavicle, the sternum and the upper six costal cartilages
structures.insertionNote: Outer lip of the groove at the front of the upper humerus
actions: Brings the arm across the chest
structures.summary: The large fan-shaped muscle of the chest, converging on the upper humerus. Its lower edge forms the front fold of the armpit.

issues.name: Pec strain or tear
issues.note: Sudden pain and bruising at the front of the armpit during a heavy press.

issues.name: Chest wall pain
issues.note: A sore chest muscle after exertion, tender to press. If unsure, get chest pain checked.

structures.name: Pectoralis minor
structures.insertionNote: Coracoid process of the shoulder blade
actions: Pulls the shoulder blade forward and down
Helps lift the ribs in deep breathing
structures.summary: A thin triangular muscle hidden under pectoralis major.

issues.name: Tight pectoralis minor
issues.note: Rounded shoulders. It can squeeze the nerves and vessels going to the arm (thoracic outlet).

structures.name: Serratus anterior
structures.originNote: Outer surfaces of ribs 1–8, in saw-tooth slips
structures.insertionNote: The inner border of the shoulder blade (front surface)
actions: Pulls the shoulder blade forward around the ribs, as in punching
Holds the shoulder blade flat against the chest wall
Rotates it upward for reaching overhead
structures.summary: Saw-toothed slips on the side of the chest that wrap around to the shoulder blade.

issues.name: Winged scapula
issues.note: If its nerve is injured, the shoulder blade sticks out when you push against a wall.

structures.name: Intercostal muscles
structures.originNote: Each rib, to the rib below it
actions: Lift and lower the ribs during breathing
structures.summary: Three thin layers of muscle filling each space between the ribs.

members.name: External intercostals
members.note: Lift the ribs as you breathe in.

members.name: Internal intercostals
members.note: Pull the ribs down when you breathe out hard.

members.name: Innermost intercostals
members.note: The deepest layer, with the nerves and vessels running between.

issues.name: Intercostal strain
issues.note: Sharp pain between the ribs after coughing fits, twisting or lifting.

issues.name: Intercostal nerve pain or shingles
issues.note: Burning pain along one rib space. A blistering rash suggests shingles.

structures.name: Diaphragm
structures.originNote: Xiphoid process, the inner surfaces of the lower six ribs and the lumbar vertebrae (the crura)
structures.insertionNote: Its own central tendon at the top of the dome
actions: The main muscle of breathing: contracting flattens the dome and draws air in
Helps raise abdominal pressure for coughing, lifting and childbirth
structures.summary: A dome-shaped sheet separating the chest from the abdomen. The esophagus, aorta and inferior vena cava pass through it.

issues.name: Hiatus hernia
issues.note: Part of the stomach slides up through the diaphragm, causing reflux.

issues.name: Hiccups
issues.note: Involuntary spasms. Hiccups lasting more than two days should be checked.

issues.name: Shoulder-tip pain
issues.note: Irritation under the diaphragm (blood, infection, gallbladder) is often felt at the tip of the shoulder.

structures.name: Rectus abdominis
structures.originNote: Pubic crest and pubic symphysis
structures.insertionNote: Xiphoid process and the cartilages of ribs 5–7
actions: Bends the trunk forward, as in sit-ups
structures.summary: The paired “six-pack” running down the front of the abdomen, crossed by tendinous bands and joined in the midline by the linea alba.

issues.name: Diastasis recti
issues.note: The two halves separate along the midline, common after pregnancy: a ridge or bulge appears when sitting up.

issues.name: Abdominal strain
issues.note: Pain on coughing, laughing or sitting up after a sudden twist or overtraining.

structures.name: External oblique
structures.originNote: Outer surfaces of ribs 5–12
structures.insertionNote: Iliac crest and pubic tubercle, and the linea alba through its broad tendon sheet
actions: Twists the trunk to the opposite side
structures.summary: The outermost flat muscle on the side of the abdomen. Its fibres run down and inward like hands in pockets, and its tendon sheet forms the inguinal ligament.

issues.name: Side strain
issues.note: Pain at the side of the waist after twisting sports.

issues.name: Inguinal hernia
issues.note: A weak spot in the groin wall formed by its tendon sheet can let a bulge through.

structures.name: Internal oblique & transversus abdominis
structures.latin: Musculus obliquus internus et transversus abdominis
structures.originNote: Iliac crest, the inguinal ligament and the thoracolumbar fascia
structures.insertionNote: The lowest ribs and the linea alba
structures.nerve: Lower intercostal, iliohypogastric and ilioinguinal nerves
structures.summary: The two deeper layers of the abdominal wall, hidden under the external oblique.

members.name: Internal oblique
members.note: Fibres run up and inward, at right angles to the external oblique.

members.name: Transversus abdominis
members.note: Horizontal fibres that wrap the abdomen like a corset.

issues.name: Weak core
issues.note: Linked with low back pain. Targeted strengthening helps many people.

structures.name: Pelvic floor muscles
structures.originNote: Inside of the pubis, the side walls of the pelvis and the ischial spines
structures.insertionNote: The coccyx and the tissue around the anus and urethra
structures.nerve: Sacral nerves (S3–S4) and the pudendal nerve
actions: Support the bladder, bowel and (in women) the uterus
Relax to let you pass urine and stool
structures.summary: A muscular hammock across the bottom of the pelvis.

members.name: Levator ani
members.note: The main sling: puborectalis, pubococcygeus and iliococcygeus.

members.name: Coccygeus
members.note: A small muscle at the back, to the coccyx.

issues.name: Stress incontinence
issues.note: Leaking when coughing, sneezing or jumping. Pelvic floor exercises help.

issues.name: Pelvic organ prolapse
issues.note: A heavy, dragging feeling or a bulge in the vagina.

issues.name: Pelvic floor tension
issues.note: Pelvic pain, painful sex or difficulty emptying when the muscles can’t relax.

structures.name: Erector spinae
structures.originNote: Sacrum, the back of the iliac crest and the lumbar spinous processes
structures.insertionNote: Ribs, thoracic and cervical vertebrae, and the mastoid process
structures.nerve: Back (dorsal) branches of the spinal nerves
structures.summary: Three columns of muscle running either side of the spine from the pelvis to the skull.

members.name: Iliocostalis
members.note: The outer column, to the ribs.

members.name: Longissimus
members.note: The middle and longest column, reaching the skull.

members.name: Spinalis
members.note: The inner column, next to the spinous processes.

issues.name: Low back strain
issues.note: Spasm and pain on bending or lifting. It usually settles within weeks, and staying gently active helps.

issues.name: Postural back pain
issues.note: Ache from long periods of sitting or standing.

structures.name: Quadratus lumborum
structures.originNote: Back of the iliac crest
structures.insertionNote: The 12th rib and the lumbar transverse processes
structures.summary: A deep, square muscle of the lower back between the pelvis, the lowest rib and the lumbar spine.

issues.name: One-sided low back pain
issues.note: Deep pain on one side, worse turning in bed or standing up from sitting.

structures.name: Biceps brachii
structures.originNote: Coracoid process (short head) and the bump above the shoulder socket (long head)
structures.insertionNote: Radial tuberosity, plus a tendon sheet onto the forearm
actions: Turns the palm up, its strongest action
structures.summary: The two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm. It crosses both the shoulder and the elbow.

issues.name: Biceps tendinopathy
issues.note: Pain at the front of the shoulder, worse lifting or reaching.

issues.name: Distal biceps rupture
issues.note: A pop at the elbow when lifting, then bruising and a weak twist (as with a screwdriver). See a doctor within days, because repair works best early.

issues.name: Long-head rupture
issues.note: A “Popeye” bulge in the upper arm, often in older adults. Usually little loss of function.

structures.name: Brachialis
structures.originNote: Lower half of the front of the humerus
structures.insertionNote: Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna
actions: The main elbow bender, whichever way the palm faces
structures.summary: It lies under the biceps and does most of the work of bending the elbow.

issues.name: Brachialis strain
issues.note: A deep ache at the front of the elbow after heavy lifting or climbing.

structures.name: Triceps brachii
structures.originNote: Just below the shoulder socket (long head) and the back of the humerus (lateral and medial heads)
structures.insertionNote: Olecranon, the point of the elbow
actions: Helps pull the arm back (long head)
structures.summary: The three-headed muscle on the back of the upper arm. From the front only its inner edge shows.

issues.name: Triceps tendinopathy
issues.note: Pain at the back of the elbow with pushing exercises.

structures.name: Brachioradialis
structures.originNote: Outer ridge of the humerus just above the elbow
structures.insertionNote: Styloid process of the radius at the wrist
actions: Bends the elbow, especially with the thumb pointing up (hammer grip)
structures.summary: The muscle forming the outer edge of the forearm, from just above the elbow to the wrist.

issues.name: Forearm strain
issues.note: Ache along the outer forearm after repetitive lifting with a hammer grip.

structures.name: Forearm flexors
structures.originNote: Inner elbow (medial epicondyle) and the front of the radius and ulna
structures.insertionNote: Wrist, palm and finger bones; pronator teres to the middle of the radius
structures.summary: The muscles on the palm side of the forearm, mostly starting from the inner elbow. Their tendons pass through the carpal tunnel.

members.name: Pronator teres
members.note: Turns the palm down; runs to the middle of the radius.

members.name: Flexor carpi radialis
members.note: Bends the wrist toward the thumb side.

members.name: Palmaris longus
members.note: A thin tendon at the centre of the wrist; absent in roughly 1 in 7 people.

members.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
members.note: Bends the wrist toward the little-finger side.

members.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
members.note: Bends the middle joints of the fingers.

members.name: Flexor digitorum profundus
members.note: Bends the fingertips.

members.name: Flexor pollicis longus
members.note: Bends the tip of the thumb.

issues.name: Golfer’s elbow
issues.note: Pain at the inner elbow with gripping and lifting.

issues.name: Trigger finger
issues.note: A flexor tendon catches in its sheath, making a finger lock.

issues.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
issues.note: Swollen flexor tendon sheaths can squeeze the median nerve at the wrist.

structures.name: Forearm extensors
structures.originNote: Outer elbow (lateral epicondyle) and the back of the radius and ulna
structures.insertionNote: Backs of the hand and finger bones
actions: Straighten and cock back the wrist and fingers
Steady the wrist so you can grip
structures.summary: The muscles on the back of the forearm, mostly starting from the outer elbow. In the front view only their outer edge shows.

members.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus & brevis
members.note: Cock the wrist back. ECRB is the usual source of tennis elbow.

members.name: Extensor digitorum
members.note: Straightens the fingers.

members.name: Extensor digiti minimi
members.note: Straightens the little finger.

members.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
members.note: Cocks the wrist toward the little-finger side.

members.name: Supinator
members.note: Turns the palm up.

members.name: Thumb muscles
members.note: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis longus & brevis move the thumb out and back.

members.name: Extensor indicis
members.note: Straightens the index finger for pointing.

issues.name: Tennis elbow
issues.note: Pain on the outer elbow when gripping, lifting a kettle or turning a handle.

issues.name: De Quervain’s tenosynovitis
issues.note: Pain on the thumb side of the wrist from two thumb tendons in this group.

structures.name: Thenar muscles
structures.originNote: Scaphoid, trapezium and the ligament roofing the carpal tunnel
structures.insertionNote: First metacarpal and the base of the thumb
actions: Bring the thumb across the palm to touch the fingertips (opposition)
structures.summary: The fleshy mound at the base of the thumb.

members.name: Abductor pollicis brevis
members.note: Moves the thumb away from the palm.

members.name: Flexor pollicis brevis
members.note: Bends the thumb.

members.name: Opponens pollicis
members.note: Rolls the thumb across to meet the fingers.

members.name: Adductor pollicis
members.note: Deep; pulls the thumb in, as in pinch grip.

issues.name: Thenar wasting
issues.note: A flattened thumb mound with a clumsy pinch can be a sign of advanced carpal tunnel syndrome.

structures.name: Hypothenar muscles
structures.originNote: Pisiform and hamate
structures.insertionNote: Fifth metacarpal and the base of the little finger
actions: Move and cup the little finger
structures.summary: The mound on the little-finger side of the palm.

members.name: Abductor digiti minimi
members.note: Spreads the little finger.

members.name: Flexor digiti minimi brevis
members.note: Bends the little finger.

members.name: Opponens digiti minimi
members.note: Cups the palm.

issues.name: Ulnar nerve compression
issues.note: Numbness of the little and ring fingers with weak hand muscles, from pressure at the elbow or the wrist (for example in cyclists).

structures.name: Iliopsoas
structures.originNote: Lumbar vertebrae (psoas) and the inside of the pelvic wing (iliacus)
structures.insertionNote: Lesser trochanter of the femur
structures.nerve: Lumbar plexus (L1–L3) and the femoral nerve
actions: The strongest hip flexor: lifts the thigh
Bends the trunk forward when the legs are fixed, as in sitting up
structures.summary: A deep muscle running from the spine and inner pelvis over the front of the hip to the femur. It is the main muscular link between the spine and the legs.

members.name: Psoas major
members.note: From the lumbar spine.

members.name: Iliacus
members.note: From the inside of the pelvic wing.

members.name: Psoas minor
members.note: Small, absent in about half of people.

issues.name: Hip flexor strain
issues.note: Deep groin pain when lifting the knee, after sprinting or kicking.

issues.name: Snapping hip
issues.note: A clunk at the front of the hip as the tendon flicks over the pelvis.

issues.name: Psoas abscess
issues.note: Rare: infection here causes fever, back or groin pain and a limp. It needs urgent care.

structures.name: Gluteus maximus
structures.originNote: Back of the ilium, the sacrum and the coccyx
structures.insertionNote: The gluteal tuberosity of the femur and, through the IT band, the tibia
actions: Extends the hip: standing up, climbing, running
structures.summary: The largest muscle in the body, forming the buttock.

issues.name: Buttock pain
issues.note: Often referred from the lower back or the sacroiliac joint; a true muscle strain is less common.

structures.name: Gluteus medius
structures.originNote: Outer surface of the ilium
structures.insertionNote: Greater trochanter
actions: Lifts the leg out to the side
Keeps the pelvis level when you stand on one leg
structures.summary: A fan-shaped hip muscle, mostly hidden behind gluteus maximus, that is vital for walking without a limp.

issues.name: Gluteal tendinopathy
issues.note: Pain on the outer hip, worse lying on that side, on stairs or standing on one leg. Common in women over 40.

issues.name: Hip drop when walking
issues.note: If it is weak, the pelvis drops on the opposite side with each step (Trendelenburg gait).

structures.name: Tensor fasciae latae
structures.originNote: Anterior superior iliac spine, the front point of the hip bone
structures.insertionNote: Through the iliotibial (IT) band onto the outer tibia
actions: Helps flex the hip and lift it outward
Tightens the IT band to steady the knee
structures.summary: A short hip muscle that tightens the iliotibial band, the tough strip running down the outside of the thigh to the knee.

issues.name: IT band syndrome
issues.note: Sharp pain on the outer knee in runners and cyclists, worse going downhill.

structures.name: Sartorius
structures.originNote: Anterior superior iliac spine
structures.insertionNote: Upper inner tibia (pes anserinus)
actions: Flexes the hip, turns it outward and bends the knee: the cross-legged “tailor” position
structures.summary: The longest muscle in the body: a strap crossing the thigh diagonally from the hip to the inner knee.

issues.name: Pes anserine bursitis
issues.note: Pain on the inner knee just below the joint, common with knee arthritis and in runners.

structures.name: Adductors
structures.originNote: Pubis and ischium
structures.insertionNote: Back of the femur and, for gracilis, the upper inner tibia
actions: Help flex and rotate the hip
structures.summary: The muscles of the inner thigh, fanning from the pubic bone to the femur.

members.name: Pectineus
members.note: The highest, next to the hip flexors.

members.name: Adductor longus
members.note: The one most often strained.

members.name: Adductor brevis
members.note: Lies under adductor longus.

members.name: Adductor magnus
members.note: The largest, reaching down to the knee.

members.name: Gracilis
members.note: A long strap down to the inner knee.

issues.name: Groin strain
issues.note: Sudden inner-thigh pain during kicking, sprinting or changing direction.

issues.name: Long-standing groin pain
issues.note: Persistent pain where the adductors attach to the pubis, common in football and hockey.

structures.name: Rectus femoris
structures.originNote: Anterior inferior iliac spine and just above the hip socket
structures.insertionNote: The patella through the quadriceps tendon, then the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament
actions: Flexes the hip (the only quadriceps muscle that crosses it)
structures.summary: The middle muscle of the quadriceps, running straight down the front of the thigh.

issues.name: Quad strain
issues.note: Sudden pain at the front of the thigh when sprinting or kicking.

issues.name: Jumper’s knee
issues.note: Pain just below the kneecap with jumping and squatting (patellar tendinopathy).

structures.name: Vastus lateralis
structures.originNote: Greater trochanter and the outer back ridge of the femur
structures.summary: The largest quadriceps muscle, forming the outer thigh.

issues.name: Dead leg
issues.note: A hard knock causes painful bruising in the thigh. Heavy, worsening swelling needs checking.

structures.name: Vastus medialis
structures.originNote: Inner back ridge of the femur
actions: Its lowest fibres help the kneecap track straight
structures.summary: The teardrop-shaped quadriceps muscle just above the inner knee.

issues.name: Kneecap tracking pain
issues.note: Weakness here is linked with pain around the kneecap.

structures.name: Vastus intermedius
structures.originNote: Front and outer surface of the femoral shaft
structures.summary: The deep quadriceps muscle, lying on the femur under rectus femoris.

structures.name: Hamstrings
structures.originNote: Ischial tuberosity (the sitting bone); the short head of biceps from the femur
structures.insertionNote: Head of the fibula and the upper inner tibia
actions: Straighten the hip, swinging the leg back
structures.summary: Three muscles on the back of the thigh, from the sitting bone to just below the knee.

members.name: Biceps femoris
members.note: The outer hamstring, with long and short heads.

members.name: Semitendinosus
members.note: The inner, with a long cord-like tendon.

members.name: Semimembranosus
members.note: The deepest inner hamstring.

issues.name: Hamstring strain
issues.note: Sudden pain at the back of the thigh while sprinting; bruising may follow.

issues.name: Hamstring tendinopathy
issues.note: Deep pain at the sitting bone, worse sitting or running uphill.

structures.name: Tibialis anterior
structures.originNote: Outer surface of the upper two-thirds of the tibia
structures.insertionNote: Medial cuneiform and the base of the first metatarsal
structures.summary: The muscle just outside the shinbone. You can feel its tendon at the front of the ankle when you lift your toes.

issues.name: Shin splints (front)
issues.note: Pain along the front-outer shin, worse at the start of a run.

issues.name: Foot drop
issues.note: If its nerve is damaged, the foot slaps or the toes catch when walking.

issues.name: Compartment syndrome
issues.note: Severe, rising pain and tightness in the front of the shin after an injury or hard exercise. It is urgent.

structures.name: Long toe extensors
structures.latin: Musculi extensores digitorum et hallucis longi
structures.originNote: Outer tibial condyle and the front of the fibula
structures.insertionNote: Tops of the toe bones
structures.summary: Long muscles on the front of the leg whose tendons fan out over the top of the foot to the toes.

members.name: Extensor digitorum longus
members.note: Lifts the four small toes.

members.name: Extensor hallucis longus
members.note: Lifts the big toe.

members.name: Fibularis tertius
members.note: A small slip that lifts the outer foot.

issues.name: Extensor tendinopathy
issues.note: Pain on the top of the foot, often from tight laces or a sudden increase in running.

structures.name: Fibularis (peroneal) muscles
structures.originNote: Outer surface of the fibula
structures.insertionNote: Bases of the first and fifth metatarsals and the medial cuneiform
structures.summary: Muscles along the outside of the leg whose tendons run behind the outer ankle bone.

members.name: Fibularis longus
members.note: Its tendon crosses under the foot to the first metatarsal.

members.name: Fibularis brevis
members.note: Inserts on the fifth metatarsal.

issues.name: Peroneal tendinopathy
issues.note: Pain and swelling behind the outer ankle, often after sprains.

issues.name: Fifth metatarsal avulsion
issues.note: Rolling the ankle can make fibularis brevis pull off a piece of bone.

structures.name: Gastrocnemius
structures.originNote: Both femoral condyles, just above the knee
structures.insertionNote: The heel bone (calcaneus), through the Achilles tendon
actions: Points the foot: rising on tiptoe and pushing off
structures.summary: The two-headed muscle forming the bulk of the calf. From the front only its inner edge shows.

issues.name: Calf strain (tennis leg)
issues.note: Sudden pain in the upper calf, as if kicked, during a push-off.

issues.name: Achilles tendinopathy
issues.note: Pain and stiffness above the heel, worst in the morning.

structures.name: Soleus
structures.originNote: Back of the upper tibia and fibula
structures.insertionNote: The heel bone (calcaneus), through the Achilles tendon
actions: Points the foot, especially with the knee bent
Pumps blood back up from the legs while walking
structures.summary: A broad, flat calf muscle under gastrocnemius. Together they form the triceps surae.

issues.name: Soleus strain
issues.note: Gradually tightening lower-calf pain in runners.

issues.name: Shin splints (inner)
issues.note: Pain along the inner edge of the shin where soleus and the deep calf muscles attach.
